text: They told us it was comfort care and my brother thought that meant giving up. He asked me twice if they had stopped trying to help her. Nobody sat us down and explained.
The night nurse did not know Dad hates the radio on, again. We had told the day team on Monday. It is a small thing but it made the whole night harder for him.
I freeze when she goes quiet and I start chattering to fill it. Then I feel silly afterwards. Is there a way to practise being still before I go in?

source_label: Comment on a post about grief
text: I never know what to write on a sympathy card without sounding cold. I end up copying a line off the internet and then I feel worse.

source_label: Comment on a post about care
text: Nobody explained what comfort care actually includes, I assumed it meant no treatment at all. Thank you for writing about it plainly.

source_label: Email from a care home manager
text: We repeat the same story to every new nurse at the changeover, and families get tired of it. Our staff change so often that details fall through.

source_label: Call with a husband caring at home
text: I have not slept more than three hours in a row since March. People tell me to look after myself and I nod, but there is no one else to do the nights.

source_label: Email from a hospice volunteer lead
text: Our volunteers say silence is the part they dread most. They sign up wanting to help and then worry they are doing nothing.
Could you write something about what the phrase comfort care really means? My mother-in-law keeps asking us to stop it, and we do not know how to answer.
There is nowhere to park near the east entrance after four. We circled for twenty minutes before the evening session started.
A one page handover card would have saved us three bad nights. Even a sheet on the wall with the likes and dislikes would have helped.

source_label: Call with a colleague of a mourner
text: My colleague's father died and I avoided her for a week because I had nothing to say. Now it feels too late to bring it up.
Her sister said I should rest but there is nobody to take my shift at the bedside. Resting feels like leaving.
The word comfort sounded soft to us, like they were just making him cosy. We did not realise it was a full plan with pain control.
What do I do with my hands when nobody is speaking? I always end up fiddling with my phone and feeling rude.
The garden volunteers made my father's last afternoon beautiful. We wanted to say thank you to whoever planted the roses.
Founder note: handover cards keep coming up in every workshop this month. Ask Ferncliffe whether we can share their template.
People keep telling me he is in a better place and I want to scream. I know they mean well but it does not help at all.
Does the course count toward continuing education credits, and is the room comfortable for a full day? I have a bad back.
Would you come on our podcast about local small business? It is a friendly half hour and we record on Thursdays.
